title: Stab wound chest - tension PTX
objectives: Seal open chest wound at once (vented/occlusive, 4.8); check back and axillae
Recognize tension PTX (4.8 criteria) and burp/remove the seal
NDT is paramedic-only (6.5): intercept only if no delay; rapid to UVMMC
Penetrating torso: fluids only to SBP 80-90 / radial / mentation (2.24A)
Scene < 10 min; TRAUMA ALERT to UVMMC Level 1 (4.9)
resources: Vented chest seal x2 (+ unvented), gauze, O2/NRB, BVM, capno, IV x2, NS. UVMMC (Level 1) ~15 min ground; paramedic intercept ETA 8 min
dispatch: UVM Rescue, respond to Bayside Apartments, 120 Blakely Rd, Colchester, for a 24-year-old male stabbed in the chest. Patient is conscious. PD is on scene. Time out 2215.

scene.location: Ground-floor apartment living room, ~15 min from UVMMC. Party breaking up; PD has the suspect outside.
scene.setup: Pt sitting on couch, leaning forward, pressing a bloody towel to L side. Kitchen knife bagged by PD.
scene.moulage: 2 cm slit L lateral chest (5th ICS, ant axillary line), bubbling; 1 cm shallow cut below L scapula; pale, sweaty.
scene.roles: Pt actor; PD officer; roommate ("medics are 8 min out, shouldn't you wait?").

patient.name: Tyler Brennan
patient.on_arrival: Upright, tripoding, 3-4 word sentences, pale, sweaty. Towel on L side, sucking sound with breaths.

SAMPLE: L chest pain, SOB, "can't get a full breath"
Stabbed L side in argument ~2205. Walked to couch

primary: Minimal external bleeding. **Open chest wound** - gloved hand over it now
RR 28, labored. Sucking wound L. L sounds decreased
Full exposure: shallow cut below L scapula. No other wounds
**HIGH**: open PTX, risk of tension. Seal, load and go
secondary: 2 cm slit L 5th ICS ant axillary line; no crepitus
Soft, non-tender (wound below nipple line - watch)
1 cm shallow cut below L scapula, oozing, no bubbles
Penetrating only, no neuro deficit -> no SMR (4.6)

vitals.other: Sucking wound L. L sounds decreased
Less distress, seal intact. Full sentences
**JVD, L sounds absent**, agitated, radial weak. Trachea midline
Distress eases, JVD less, L sounds faint

vitals.trigger: IF not burped by ~T+13, or burp fails
vitals.other: Shallow, cyanotic, radial absent, trachea shifted R. Peri-arrest

flow.give: Read dispatch. PD: "One stab wound, left side." Pt tripoding, towel on L chest.
Stage **A**. Show WOUND card. BACK card only if back checked.

branches.if: Unvented seal taped on all 4 sides

expected: Back and axillae checked; back cut dressed

flow.give: Roommate: "Medics are 8 min out, shouldn't you wait for them?" UVMMC 15 min.

branches.if: Rapid load; intercept met en route

expected: Position of comfort, upright; no SMR (4.6)

expected.text: Intercept en route only, no delay (4.8)

flow.give: Stage **C** in rig. Show NECK / L CHEST card. Pt: "It's getting worse!"

branches.if: Not recognized; BVM / more O2 only
Burp fails: wound clotted, no air rush
branches.then: Stage **E** values; expect rapid UVMMC, Med Direction, NDT only via intercept (6.5)

expected: Tension recognized (4.8: distress + shock + JVD/absent sounds)
Reassess sounds, SpO2, BP after burp

flow.give: Intercept meets you 6 min from UVMMC. Pt asks for "the gas" for pain.

branches.then: SBP 120s, then more bleeding; debrief 2.24A target
expect gloved hand, new seal, reassess for tension

expected.text: IV x2 en route; 250 mL only if SBP < 80-90 / no radial / AMS

expected: Seal + breath sounds rechecked q5; burp as needed

expected.text: Medic rides in; no vehicle transfer delay

expected: MIST: wound sites, seal type, burp times

expected.text: SIREN incl. back wound and tension timeline

critical: Open chest wound not sealed promptly (4.8)
Back / axillae not checked for more wounds
Tension signs not recognized / seal not burped (4.8)
Scene delayed waiting for intercept (4.8: minimize scene time)
No TRAUMA ALERT / not direct to UVMMC Level 1 (4.9)
Unrestricted fluids in penetrating torso trauma (2.24A)
Nitrous oxide given with chest trauma (2.20A)
differentials: Distress, shock, JVD, absent L sounds
JVD (flat veins expected); air rush on burp
debrief: Which findings told you this became a tension PTX?
Why burp the seal instead of bagging harder?
Why not wait for the medic who was 8 min out?
What fluid target did you use, and why for penetrating torso?
Why no collar for this patient?

crew_card.dispatch: Bayside Apartments, 120 Blakely Rd, Colchester. 24 y/o M stabbed in the chest, conscious. PD on scene.
crew_card.on_arrival: Young man on a couch, leaning forward, holding a bloody towel to his L side, breathing fast. PD officer with him.

actor_card.Act: Short sentences, gasping. Lean forward. "I can't get a breath."
actor_card.Wound uncovered: Breathe noisily; hiss/suck sound with each breath.
actor_card.Getting worse (~T+10): More panic: "It's getting worse!" Then stop talking, gasp.
actor_card.If never burped: Eyes close, respond only to loud voice.
actor_card.Ask: "Am I gonna die? Don't call my mom."

show_cards.title: WOUND - L CHEST
show_cards.body:
2 cm slit, side of L chest under the arm, 5th rib space.
Bubbles and a sucking sound with each breath.
Little bleeding.

show_cards.title: BACK
show_cards.body:
1 cm shallow cut below L shoulder blade.
Oozing. No bubbles.
show_cards.cue: Give only when crew checks the back

show_cards.title: NECK / L CHEST
show_cards.body:
Neck veins swollen.
L chest: no air movement heard.
R chest: clear.
Trachea midline.
show_cards.cue: Give at Stage C (~T+10). Burp -> rush of air, L sounds faint (Stage D)

moulage_tags.text: 2 cm cut; bubbles and sucking sound with breaths

moulage_tags.cue: Swap to 'Neck veins swollen' at Stage C
Stage C: L silent. Stage D: L faint
Stage C: weak. Stage E: absent
